summary: STOP CONDITION 1 fired. The seam miss is by MORE than a tolerance band (positions genuinely differ), the packet's own predicate for fix (a)/(c). Direction (b) (widen the weld) is disproved by direct measurement: welds from the test tolerance up to 5e-2 NORMALIZED leave bottle Irregular, punched-cube Oriented, torus-punched-cube Oriented and sphere Irregular (only the torus, cube and cube-in-cube close at 5e-2). Direction (a) was attempted at its minimal form (densify the shared per-edge discretization the legacy shell/cshell paths already feed every face, LEGACY const with tol/8) and empirically does NOT produce seam agreement: a curved carrier re-samples its boundary independently of the shared edge density, so the planar cap and curved wall of the in-memory special_cylinder fixture still carry different, topologically interleaved sample sets along their shared circle at every tested shared density (at the stock density the cap ring = the shared polyline's 15 deg chain; the wall ring = that SAME shared 15 deg chain PLUS an intrinsic ~7.83 deg chain that is invariant under 8x shared densification). Leftover seam chains are therefore interleaved rather than offset, so no positional merge (b) and no index-only closure (c) can bridge them; closing them requires making each face's seam sample set a pure function of the shared edge (the certified (EdgeID, ordinal) discipline) inside the per-face boundary pipeline, which is a structural change to the face tessellation contract that cannot be landed as a bounded in-scope edit and was not reachable within this packet's budget. No code change is committed (the working tree carries only this RESULT).

deviation_notes: STOP CONDITION 1 (verbatim from the packet): 'The diagnosis shows the seam miss is by MORE than a tolerance band (positions genuinely differ) -> the fix is (a) or (c); if neither is reachable without touching truck-topology, SPEC_GAP naming the boundary.' TRIGGERED. Instrumented diagnosis (in-process, per-fixture, pre/post weld, at the reading pipeline the tests use: triangulate 0.01 + put_together(TOLERANCE*2) + remove_degenerate_faces + remove_unused_attrs) with counts for special_cylinder-shell / special_cylinder-cshell / bottle / punched-cube / torus-punched-cube / sphere / torus (solid and csolid identical for the compressed fixtures): post-weld-undirected-indexpair multiplicities show ONLY count-1 (unpaired boundary) and count-2-opposite (sealed) pairs - no same-direction duplicates, no 3+ uses - so the unclosed remainder is a pure unmatched-boundary problem (Oriented), except the sphere (Regular: pairs appearing twice in the SAME direction) and the bottle (Irregular: pairs reaching 3+ uses) whose structural leftovers are welding-independent. Boundary edges remaining after the weld+clean at tolerance 5e-2: bottle 39 (isolated chains at the revolution axis), punched-cube 24 (hole-ring chains), torus-punched-cube 24, sphere 262 (pole-side fragments), torus 0; at the test tolerance 2e-6: bottle 48/41, punched-cube 24/24, torus-punched-cube 66/66, sphere 717/717, torus 284/284 (solid/csolid). Welding therefore closes only the torus; widening the weld (b) is necessary but not sufficient and cannot be the fix. Seam-twin position errors are not roundoff-scale: leftover seam chains have no counterpart vertex within their own neighborhood (special_cylinder wide-open boundary edges report nearest other segment > 1e-4 on a unit model; sphere/torus up to ~0.9), i.e. mechanism (a) seam parameterization mismatch (per-face sample counts on the shared curve differ), exactly as the packet's mechanism paragraph predicts - but the mismatch is created AFTER the shared-edge discretization (per-carrier boundary re-sampling inside each face), which the packet's preferred (a) form ('transplant the certified (EdgeID, ordinal) discipline') must therefore key on more than the shared polyline alone.

Direction (a) minimal attempt, evidence that it is not reachable as a bounded change: raising shared-edge discretization density 8x at all three legacy edge-creation sites (shell_tessellation, shell_tessellation_single_thread, cshell_tessellation_inner) moved the special_cylinder cap ring from 24 to 64 samples and the shared chain inside the wall ring from 15 deg to 5.6 deg spacing, but the wall ring STILL contains an additional, independent ~7.83 deg chain at BOTH densities, and the leftover boundary count grew (special_cylinder-shell 177 -> 280 directed edges). Conclusion: a curved face's final seam vertex set is not the shared edge polyline; some per-carrier boundary stage (not the shared discretization) injects its own samples, so shared-edge densification cannot make adjacent faces agree. Localizing that stage and re-routing it onto a per-edge (EdgeID, ordinal) contract - or replacing the legacy positional weld with a recorded seam-chain closure that also subdivides the coarser face's seam polygons to the finer neighbor's sample set - is the real fix; both require restructuring the per-face boundary/assembly pipeline and were not completable within this packet's turn budget.

Per-face seam-density audit (decisive instrument, special_cylinder fixture-INDEPENDENT repro): cap face0 ring vertices = exactly the shared arc polyline samples (24/full ring at the stock density); wall face2/face3 ring vertices = the shared polyline samples PLUS an intrinsic chain, giving 35/half-ring for each wall vs 12/half-ring for the cap. Adjacent faces along one shared circle therefore emit different sample counts, so after any positional weld the cap's coarse edges and the wall's fine edges are both unpaired and interleave along the seam (leftover boundary wires alternate fine and coarse vertices along z=0/z=1 rings; the wall-wall vertical seams and the planar-only fixtures seal).

evidence.deciding_experiment: Removing per-carrier seam re-sampling is required for (a); because it could not be isolated in budget, and because leftover seam chains are interleaved (no coincident vertices to merge, no index closure possible) and include welding-independent Regular/Irregular structures (sphere/bottle), neither (a) nor (c) was reachable as a bounded, verifiable in-scope change.

stop_conditions_checked.stop_condition_1_seam_miss_is_more_than_: TRIGGERED and documented above: leftover seam chains from adjacent analytic faces carry genuinely different sample parameterizations (differing sample counts along the shared curve), are interleaved rather than offset, and are not closable by any weld tolerance up to 5e-2 normalized. The packet's mandated fix is (a) or (c); (a)'s minimal bounded form (shared-edge density) is empirically insufficient because a curved carrier re-samples its boundary independently of the shared polyline, and a full per-edge (EdgeID, ordinal) seam-sample contract or a seam-strip polygon-subdivision closure is a structural change to the face tessellation pipeline that was not reachable within this packet's turn budget. SPEC_GAP: the boundary of the gap is the per-face boundary sample construction inside truck-meshalgo/src/tessellation (PolyBoundaryPiece/try_new lift and the per-carrier stages between the shared edge discretization and the CDT boundary map); truck-topology itself was not implicated and is not the boundary.

recommended_amendment: Re-file DEF-TESS-ANALYTIC-SEAM (or a successor defect) scoped to one of two structural fixes, both inside truck-meshalgo/src/tessellation/: (A) make every face's seam sample set a pure function of the shared topological edge - route the per-carrier boundary samples through an (EdgeID, ordinal)-keyed seam contract so adjacent faces on the same edge emit identical (exactly-coincident) seam vertices and the existing positional weld closes them exactly like the planar seams do (the certified path's discipline); or (B) add a recorded seam-chain closure pass on the assembled legacy polygon that, for each unmatched seam chain, subdivides the coarser face's seam polygons at the finer neighbor's seam vertices and merges the coincident vertices by index, recording every closure (the packet's direction (c), made density-aware). Either fix must also address the welding-independent Regular/ Irregular structures the sphere and bottle exhibit (same-direction duplicated index pairs and 3+ edge uses that persist through 5e-2 welds). Budget note for the re-file: this packet consumed its full 70-turn / 180k-token budget on diagnosis and the (b)-disproof and (a)-minimal-experiment documented above; the remaining work is the seam-contract restructure itself.
